QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_98

question.text: Using the same order book (Best Buy Rs. 998/200, Rs. 997/300; Best Sell Rs. 1,002/150, Rs. 1,003/350) and an ideal price of Rs. 1,000, if a trader wants to SELL 400 shares, what is the impact cost for the sell order?

explanation.text: The Logic: Step-by-step calculation: To SELL 400 shares, hit the buy side of the order book: - 200 shares at Rs. 998 = Rs. 1,99,600 - 200 shares at Rs. 997 = Rs. 1,99,400 - Total proceeds = Rs. 3,99,000 - Average sell price = 3,99,000 / 400 = Rs. 997.50 Impact cost for the sell = (Ideal price - Actual execution price) / Ideal price x 100 = (1,000 - 997.50) / 1,000 x 100 = 0.25% The Trap: Impact cost is not zero just because the trade is a sell; for a sell, execution price is below the ideal price, so impact cost = (Ideal - Execution) / Ideal x 100. Note: Pages 23-24 of the Series VIII workbook support the sell-side impact-cost method used above.
